draft.emotion: warm and familiar, speaking of family with natural affection
notes: Used to refer to an older biological sister (as opposed to 'chị', which is also used as a pronoun for any slightly older woman). In direct address, people usually just say 'chị'.

examples.translation: My older sister is a teacher.
examples.emotion: proud and fond, introducing a family member

faults.why: Wrong tones and consonant: 'chị' has nặng tone, 'gái' starts with /ɣ/, not /ŋ/.

faults.quote: when you specifically want to emphasize that your older sibling is female.
faults.why: 'Chị' is already exclusively female; 'gái' distinguishes blood sister from general 'chị' (older woman/pronoun).
